children: shares slipped 1% Thursday as rising competition from Chinese automakers adds pressure across electric vehicles, hybrids, gasoline cars and automotive software, according to a Thursday report.

Chinese manufacturers are expanding overseas as weaker domestic demand pushes them toward international markets. Their exports now include lower-cost combustion and hybrid models, while companies such as Huawei are helping local automakers add advanced driving and digital functions.

Tesla faces a broader challenge because China is both a key production base and an important sales market. Shipments from its Shanghai factory have increasingly been directed abroad as domestic competition from companies including BYD, Xiaomi and Xpeng weighs on Tesla's position at home.

The company also faces restrictions involving vehicle data collected in China, which could complicate efforts to use that information for global artificial-intelligence and autonomous-driving development. At the same time, regulatory tensions between Washington and Beijing add another layer of uncertainty for Tesla's operations.

China has also gained influence over vehicle standards, including a recall affecting 4.3 million vehicles over hidden emergency door handles, further illustrating the regulatory risks facing global automakers.

title: Tesla Stock Slips as China's Auto Attack Expands Beyond EVs
